final_recommendation: The room converged on a Wednesday USTR filing of a final protocol amendment with binding labor enforcement (60-day investigations, 5-15% automatic tariffs, direct union complaint access). Democrats committed to vote yes contingent on receipt of final text; Mexico committed to filing with sovereignty protections intact; business and media coordinated public announcement timing to lock momentum.
minority_objections: Canada demanded written side letter guaranteeing no reopening of dairy/Chapter 19 before signing off
Mexico insisted investigations remain Mexico-led with no U.S. monitors in facilities
Initial Democratic hesitation on whether protocol would survive legal challenge
key_conflicts: Mexico sovereignty vs. U.S. enforcement monitoring (resolved: Mexico-led inspections, U.S. gets reports only)
Democrats demanding binding treaty text vs. Mexico's timeline constraints (resolved: Wednesday filing commitment)
Business lobby demanding immediate public announcement vs. Democrats wanting text review first
Canada's fear of precedent for reopening other chapters vs. need to amend labor provisions
key_concessions: Mexico accepted binding 60-day investigation triggers and automatic 5-15% tariff escalation
Mexico accepted direct union complaint access to joint committee
U.S. accepted Mexico-led inspections without U.S. monitors in facilities
All parties accepted Wednesday filing deadline as hard commitment
Mexico agreed to trilateral side letter clarifying labor-only scope to address Canada's reopening concerns
red_lines: Mexico: no U.S. inspectors on Mexican soil or monitors in facilities
Democrats: protocol must be binding treaty text, not side letter
Canada: no reopening of dairy concessions or Chapter 19
Democrats: automatic tariff triggers with no discretion or consultation escape clauses
Business lobby: need firm filing date, not 'this week' target
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Whether 218 House votes are actually locked or contingent on unstated conditions beyond protocol text
Senate ratification timeline and potential obstacles not discussed
Implementation capacity in Mexico to meet 60-day timelines once mechanism is live
Potential for legal challenges to tariff automaticity despite lawyer's assurances
Political risk in Mexico if domestic opposition frames enforcement as sovereignty loss
downstream_risk_variables: Actual vote count materialization after Wednesday filing
Canada's domestic political ability to defend protocol without reopening dairy
Mexico's labor ministry capacity to execute 60-day investigations under binding deadlines
Business community's sustained support if implementation creates uncertainty
Media narrative stability if filing slips or legal challenges emerge post-ratification
uncertainty_notes: Room achieved procedural convergence on Wednesday filing and protocol terms, but actual vote mobilization remains conditional and untested. Democrats committed to 'yes' but hedged with 'once we see final text' language. Canada's side letter requirement was addressed but not finalized. Whether 218 House votes materialize, and whether Senate ratification proceeds smoothly, remain open questions. Mexico's sovereignty concerns were accommodated but implementation pressure may resurface.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Democrats repeatedly conditioned votes on binding protocol text; 'my members vote yes only if this is airtight'; entire meeting structured around unlocking ratification via amendment
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: 60-day timelines, automatic tariffs, direct union access dominated every round; 'my caucus needs the enforcement mechanism in the treaty text itself'; drove protocol design
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Business demanded firm Wednesday date and public announcement to mobilize members; 'our members need certainty before they mobilize for passage'; but not the dominant driver
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Canada insisted on side letter preventing dairy/Chapter 19 reopening; 'politically I can't sell ratification if there's even a whisper'; genuine concern but secondary to labor
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Mexico's red line on U.S. monitors in facilities; 'we don't accept foreign monitors'; resolved via Mexico-led inspections but shaped protocol design throughout
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Media actor pressed for vote commitments and announcement timing; 'workers are watching'; 'if you're still hedging the public sees weakness'; real but supporting role
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Entire meeting premised on protocol amendment as necessary for ratification; 'the package likely needs amendment to pass' was the operating assumption driving all negotiations
